frames.narration: The suite has 32 tests. Four fail now and then for dull reasons: shared state, the clock, and two fixed sleeps. A fifth hides a real race that fails about 1 attempt in 20. Run 200 times with nothing done about it.
68 of the 200 builds go red. 54 are false alarms, and the real bug appears 14 times among them. Developers start to re-run and merge, which is how trust in the build drains away.
The team adds 2 automatic retries. Now every build is green: 0 red. It feels like a fix.

But the real race failed 14 times on the first attempt, and each time a retry passed. A bug that fails 1 time in 20 almost never fails 3 times in a row, so the build never reports it. All 14 are hidden and the bug ships.
Quarantine does the same by another road. The flaky tests are taken out of the gate, and the race test went with them, because it looked flaky too. 0 red builds, and again 14 real failures hidden.

Now fix the causes: give each test its own state, inject a fake clock, and poll for the job instead of sleeping. The four noisy tests become stable. The suite is cheaper to run too, 10,617 units against 13,600.
14 builds are red, and every one is the real bug: 0 false alarms. A red build means something again, and the race is reported the 14 times it appears.
